addresses.name: CSubUnitEntry::BuildTooltip
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSubUnitEntry::BuildTooltip(CSubUnitEntry* this, GuiTooltipText* out, CGuiObject* element)
addresses.comment: **Slot 13** of CSubUnitEntry (vftable 0x15D88CC): UNIT_COMBAT_WIDTH, UNIT_CAN_UPGRADE_TO, BRIGADE_UPGRADE_MIL_CON_INFO, BRIGADE_UPGRADE_INHERITED_EXP, UW_RESERVE_INFO, UW_MOBILIZED_RESERVE_INFO. Extent 0x7493B0..0x749EDC, `ret 8` with six of them in the body. It builds GuiTooltipText records as locals and uses their copy constructor and destructor (0x7495F3/0x7495FA, 0x74999E/0x7499A5), which is a second, independent sighting of that type's members. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md. **Read whole 2026-10-12.** unit_cw_strip UNIT_COMBAT_WIDTH; upgrade_button UNIT_CAN_UPGRADE_TO and each type the played country may still build; unitstatus_reserve UW_RESERVE_INFO (VAL minus RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE x 100) or UW_MOBILIZED_RESERVE_INFO; anything else the brigade's summary (0x5A9900). An upgrade row: BRIGADE_UPGRADE_MIL_CON_INFO FROM/TO, delayed BRIGADE_UPGRADE_INHERITED_EXP. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpaneltooltips.md, section 7.

addresses.name: BuildAttritionTooltip
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall BuildAttritionTooltip(CProvince* province, Hoi3CString* out, CUnit* unit) @EAX
addresses.comment: **Attrition broken into its causes**: TERRAIN_ATTRITION, ATTR_INFRA, ATTR_WEATHER, ATTR_TECH, plus IN_FRIENDLY_FOR_ATT, IN_HOSTILE_FOR_ATT and IN_FRONT_PROV_ONLY_10. Extent 0x4A0BA0..0x4A1CCB, `ret 0xC`, one caller 0x75AEF7 inside CUnitStatusEntry slot 13 (0x35AE20). [ebp+0x10] is a polymorphic object asked its slot 9 at 0x4A0BEE; **false empties the out string and returns at once**, so the whole tooltip is gated on it. [ebp+0xC] is the out Hoi3CString and the function constructs it (0x4A0BF8). The first argument was not identified. The several `mov byte [reg+0x58],1` inside are locals - sub-tooltips - not the out. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md. **Read whole 2026-10-12**: arguments the province, the out string, the unit. Friendly not front: IN_FRIENDLY_FOR_ATT alone; front IN_FRONT_PROV_ONLY_10 (base 0.1); hostile IN_HOSTILE_FOR_ATT (base 1); then ATTR_INFRA, ATTR_WEATHER, the terrain's, ATTR_TECH and TERRAIN_ATTRITION lines. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpaneltooltips.md, section 11.

addresses.name: BuildSpeedModifierTooltip
addresses.signature: void __stdcall BuildSpeedModifierTooltip(CUnit* unit, Hoi3CString* out)
addresses.comment: **A unit's movement speed broken into its nine causes**, one line each: SPEED_MODIFIER (the total), _COMBAT, _FUEL, _TERRAIN, _TRAIT, _ADJACIENCY (the game's spelling), _WEATHER, _LOCAL_MOD, _MOTORIZED_BONUS, _RETREATING, every one with $PERC$. Extent 0x5C82A0..0x5C8CEB, `ret 8`, one caller 0x75CE5E. It calls 0x5C8D10 once at 0x5C82D4 - its immediate neighbour - passing both the value of [ebp+8] and **its address**, then re-reads [ebp+8] afterwards, so that argument is written through. **Which of the two stack arguments is the out record and which the unit is not established**; one of them is a GuiTooltipText (+0x58 written at 0x5C85B5). Nothing the simulation stores, so for BiceLib this is read-rather-than-recompute. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md. **Read whole 2026-10-12**: the unit first, the out string second. SPEED_MODIFIER and, for each term not 1, `\n- ` and its line, the term worked out as MovementSpeedModifier does. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpaneltooltips.md, section 11.

addresses.name: CUnit::GetCombinedArmsBonus
addresses.signature: int* __thiscall CUnit::GetCombinedArmsBonus(CUnit* this, int* out, int unused)
addresses.comment:
**The whole of BM_COMBINED_ARMS (0x12)**, called from CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers at 0x16A574 and only when this->+0x1CC is above zero.

    base   = this->base_ca_bonus (+0x1CC)
    ts     = resolve(this->+0x290 ? +0x28C : +0x124)->CTechnologyStatus (+0xDF8)
    groups = sum of ts->+0x5C[g] for every group index g set in this->+0x1D0..+0x1D4
    *out   = GetTraitEffect(this, 9 combined_arms_bonus) + groups + base

+0x1CC and the group bitmap at +0x1D0 are both built by the definition rebuild at 0x1B5ED0: for every group present with its CCombinedArmsGroup's +0x24 byte set, +0x1CC accumulates that group's +0x28. **Its third argument is an out string** (2026-10-12): where given and the bonus is not 0 it writes CA_BONUS_DETAILS_TOTAL, _BASE, _TECH and _TRAIT lines, each VAL times 100 to 2 places. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpaneltooltips.md, section 12.

addresses.name: CLeader::BuildTooltip
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CLeader::BuildTooltip(CLeader* this, Hoi3CString* out)
addresses.comment: **Slot 9** of CLeader (vftable 0x15C5220) and CNullLeader (0x15C524C). LEADER_SKILL or LEADER_SKILL_AT_MAX, LEADER_XP, LEADER_COMMAND_SIZE, LEADER_POSITIONING, SHIPS_LABEL/PLANES_LABEL, ACTUAL_TRAITS_DESC and TO_GAIN_TRAITS_DESC. Extent 0x580220..0x5817A0, `ret 4`, out an Hoi3CString at [ebp+8] which it constructs. **It is the caller of CTraitGainTracker::BuildProgressTooltip at 0x58161F** (rva 0x18161F, as the record already had), so the trait-gain progress lines are its TO_GAIN_TRAITS_DESC block. Safe to call on a CLeader pointer. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md. **Read whole 2026-10-12**: the rank's name, ` §Y`, his name; the command size for a fleet or air leader; an admiral's positioning; LEADER_SKILL (and LEADER_SKILL_AT_MAX); LEADER_XP; ACTUAL_TRAITS_DESC with `\n- §Y` each trait; TO_GAIN_TRAITS_DESC with the progress lines. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpaneltooltips.md, section 13.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole; the heading and skill joins in the listing.
